section: Panchayati Raj and urban bodies in Andhra Pradesh - structure, elections, finances, performance
subsections: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations
Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh according to the APSES 2025–26 figures:
1. There are 17 Municipal Corporations.
2. There are 76 Municipalities.
3. There are 30 Nagar Panchayats.
4. The total number of Urban Local Bodies is 123.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: 17 Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 30 Nagar Panchayats make a total of 123 Urban Local Bodies.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement against the table before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s: The APSES 2024–25 figures recorded which of the following combinations for Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The APSES 2024–25 figures recorded 17 Municipal Corporations and 79 Municipalities within the total of 123 Urban Local Bodies.
accepted.tq: Compare the year attached to the figures instead of treating changing counts as permanent facts.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s:
With reference to Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Elections are due in 100 of the 123 Urban Local Bodies.
2. The remaining 23 Urban Local Bodies are involved in court cases.
3. The proposed merger of 23 Municipalities is to be taken up before the elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The proposed merger of 23 Municipalities has been deferred until after the elections, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Watch for the time-sequence trap in the phrase ‘before the elections’.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s: The proposed merger of 23 Municipalities in Andhra Pradesh has been deferred until:
o: the completion of the delimitation process
the constitution of a new State Election Commission
the publication of the next Census
accepted.x: The proposed merger has been deferred until after the elections.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact stage at which the administrative action is scheduled to occur.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s: The State Election Commission of Andhra Pradesh has notified electoral rolls for how many Urban Local Bodies?
accepted.x: Electoral rolls have been notified for 41 Urban Local Bodies.
accepted.tq: Separate the number of bodies with notified rolls from the total number of Urban Local Bodies.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s: The 41 Urban Local Bodies for which electoral rolls were notified comprise:
accepted.x: The notified rolls cover 12 Corporations and 29 Municipalities or Nagar Panchayats, together making 41 Urban Local Bodies.
accepted.tq: Split the total into its two stated components before choosing the combination.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s: The electoral rolls notified for 41 Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh are due on:
accepted.x: The electoral rolls are due on 22 September 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the publication or reporting date from the date on which the rolls are due.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Proddatur is included among the Municipalities or Nagar Panchayats for which rolls were notified; it is not listed as a named Municipal Corporation in this context. Greater Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati are named Corporations.
accepted.tq: Find the location or classification mismatch among closely related urban bodies.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s: The nodal agency for all 123 Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh is the:
o: Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department
accepted.x: The Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department is the nodal agency for all 123 Urban Local Bodies.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘which department handles this subject?’ method to identify the nodal authority.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s: Which of the following places is NOT included among the named Municipal Corporations in recent reports?
accepted.x: Nandyal is mentioned among the Municipalities or Nagar Panchayats, whereas Kurnool, Guntur and Vijayawada are named Municipal Corporations.
accepted.tq: Classify each place by its urban-body category rather than by name recognition alone.
accepted.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Sarpanch from the Panchayat Secretary in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Sarpanch is the elected political head, while the Panchayat Secretary is the executive functionary.
The Sarpanch is the executive functionary, while the Secretary is the elected political head.
Both are appointed executive functionaries of the State Government.
Both are directly elected by the Gram Sabha.
accepted.x: The Sarpanch is the elected political head of the Gram Panchayat, whereas the Panchayat Secretary is the executive functionary responsible for administration.
accepted.tq: Separate political leadership from administrative execution in local government.
accepted.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Sarpanch of a Gram Panchayat is:
o: elected indirectly by the Panchayat Secretary
accepted.x: The Sarpanch is directly elected by the voters in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the mode of election of the village-level chairperson, which is left to State legislation.
accepted.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

accepted.s: Which of the following is an obligatory function of a Gram Panchayat?
accepted.x: Sanitation, drinking water, drains, street lighting, village roads and burial grounds are obligatory functions. Tree planting, libraries and markets are examples of discretionary functions.
accepted.tq: Classify the function according to whether the law makes it compulsory or dependent on available funds.
accepted.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a discretionary function of a Gram Panchayat?
accepted.x: Tree planting is a discretionary function dependent on available funds. Village roads, street lighting and drains are obligatory functions.
accepted.tq: Find the function that depends on funds rather than being compulsory under the Act.
accepted.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

accepted.s: The Gram Sabha consists of:
o: the Sarpanch and Panchayat Secretary alone
all elected members of the Gram Panchayat only
all government employees posted in the village
all registered voters of the Panchayat area
accepted.x: The Gram Sabha consists of all persons registered as voters in the area of the Panchayat.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the general body of registered voters from the elected Panchayat body.
accepted.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

accepted.s:
With reference to the Gram Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. Article 243A recognises the Gram Sabha.
2. The powers and functions of the Gram Sabha are fixed by State law.
3. The Gram Sabha consists only of elected Panchayat representatives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Gram Sabha consists of all registered voters of the Panchayat area, not merely elected representatives.
accepted.tq: Reject the composition trap that substitutes elected representatives for all registered voters.
accepted.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

accepted.s: Under Article 243C, the mode of election of the chairperson at the village level is left to the:
accepted.x: Article 243C leaves the mode of election of the village-level chairperson to the State Legislature. Chairpersons at the intermediate and district levels are elected indirectly.
accepted.tq: Identify which constitutional authority is empowered to determine the election method.
accepted.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 243K — State Election Commission for local-body elections
Article 243A — Constitution of the State Election Commission
accepted.x: Article 243K provides the constitutional basis for the State Election Commission in relation to Panchayat elections; Article 243ZA relates to municipal elections.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional article with its precise local-government subject.
accepted.sec: AP State Election Commission

accepted.s: The constitutional basis for the State Election Commission in relation to Municipal elections is provided by:
accepted.x: Article 243ZA provides the constitutional basis for the State Election Commission’s role in Municipal elections.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the closely related constitutional provisions for Panchayats and Municipalities.
accepted.sec: AP State Election Commission

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the State Election Commission under Articles 243K and 243ZA?
o: Direction and control of electoral rolls
Appointment of all Sarpanches after elections
accepted.x: The State Election Commission supervises, directs and controls electoral rolls and local-body elections, including republication of Gram Panchayat rolls. It does not appoint Sarpanches after elections.
accepted.tq: Find the option that assigns an electoral authority a post-election appointment power.
accepted.sec: AP State Election Commission

accepted.s:
The functions of the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission include:
1. Superintendence, direction and control of electoral rolls.
2. Conduct of elections to local bodies.
3. Rearrangement and republication of Gram Panchayat rolls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three are functions of the State Election Commission under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
accepted.tq: Look for the complete set when every statement describes an electoral-roll or election-control function.
accepted.sec: AP State Election Commission

accepted.s: As provided in the stated reservation framework, the reservation for Backward Classes is:
o: 34% in rural local bodies and 33⅓% in Urban Local Bodies
33⅓% in rural local bodies and 34% in Urban Local Bodies
34% in both rural and Urban Local Bodies
50% in rural local bodies and 34% in Urban Local Bodies
accepted.x: The BC quota is 34% in rural bodies and 33⅓% in Urban Local Bodies. The SC/ST quotas remain unchanged.
accepted.tq: Compare the percentages by institutional setting and avoid reversing the two figures.
accepted.sec: AP State Election Commission

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding reservation in local bodies is correct?
o: Women’s reservation is fixed at exactly 50% in every State.
SC/ST seats are allotted without reference to population.
SC/ST seats are allotted in proportion to population and by rotation.
accepted.x: SC/ST reservation is provided in proportion to population, with seats allotted by rotation. Constitutional provision requires not less than one-third reservation for women, while many States have raised it to 50%.
accepted.tq: Separate the constitutional minimum for women from the population-based and rotational rule for SC/ST seats.
accepted.sec: AP State Election Commission
